---
title: "The Reviewer's Code"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
**Prerequisites:** Send Small, Say So. **Objective:** review work that involved an LLM, kindly and effectively, and choose formats that review well.
**Time:** about 15 minutes. <span class="ao-badge">General practice, not a vendor claim. Team norms you agree locally override these defaults.</span>
:::

You will also be on the receiving end. Reviewing LLM-assisted work is the same craft as any review, with a few shifts in attention.

- **Ask for the evidence, not the story.** "Which test shows this works?" is better than "are you sure?".
- **Watch for the usual tells.** Plausible but unused code, tests weakened to pass, and confident comments that do not match the code.
- **Ask for understanding.** "Can you explain why this branch exists?" is fair for any author.
- **Say when it is too big.** "Please split this" is a legitimate review comment, and the Wall of Output taught why.
- **Be kind.** The aim is better science, not catching a person out.

## Formats that review well

Notebooks are an example. A [marimo](https://marimo.io/) notebook is stored as a plain `.py` file, so a diff shows what changed. A Jupyter `.ipynb` is JSON that also stores outputs and run counts, so diffs are noisy and hard to read. If you ask an agent to produce analysis, prefer a format your reviewer can actually diff.
